title: Not All Instructions Are Forgotten Equal
summary: I wanted to know why LLMs follow some instructions for a whole session but drop others within a few turns. So I measured it: 5 models, 12 instruction types, 3 real codebases, fit with a Bayesian hierarchical ordered-logit model. Some instructions stuck about 10x more reliably than others, and one type actually got worse the more the model was reinforced on it.
note: The benchmark behind it is open source, built on Inspect AI (UK AISI's eval framework): deterministic checkers plus a panel of LLM judges from different model families. Code's almost ready to release.
